question.problem: Consider two random variables $X$ and $Y$ with expectations $\text{E}[X]=3,$ $\text{E}[Y]=1,$ mixed moment $\text{E}[XY]=4,$ and second raw moments $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]=10$ and $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]=4.$ Find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2},
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =10-{3}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =4-{1}^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now lets find $\text{Cov}[X,Y]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =4-3\cdot 1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
